text:
Devon: quick sync — we still have the authz-graph cache serving reads in the edge layer, right? noticed a user reported access after token revoke.
Sasha: yes, edge has an LRU with 5m TTL by default. designed for p99 latency.
Hao: do we invalidate on revoke events? we publish a change event to kafka but edge picks up via polling + delta-sync.
Devon: it looks like there's a ~30s window where revoked grants still show up — customer hit it.
Chris: that's the delta-sync lag; consumers poll every 10s but we batch changes and sometimes coalesce, adds extra delay.
Maria: is that acceptable for user-facing revokes? regulators might want faster.
Devon: we need to quantify. also worried about cross-project delegation where revoke for one project still allowed via cached org-level role.
Hao: two quick knobs: reduce TTL to 30s, or wire up a push-invalidation via websocket/longpoll from change-proxy. both have tradeoffs.
Chris: TTL30 increases cache churn and backend load. push requires stable connections from many edge nodes and adds complexity to change-proxy.
Alex: can we hybrid: push invalidation for explicit revokes (admin actions) and keep periodic for routine role changes?
Sasha: that seems reasonable. admin-revoke is rare but high priority. implementation: on revoke, write to 'authz-invalidate' topic with token/user+scope. edge subscribes and evicts immediate.
Devon: how do we ensure ordering? if a grant is re-added quickly after revoke we might evict wrong state.
Hao: include a monotonic revision number in the invalidate event and the full graph snapshot id. edge compares revision before evicting.
Maria: also need to avoid leaking org->project edges during eviction. suggested payload: {type: "evict", target: "user:U123", scope: "org:O45/project:P9", rev: 9876}
Chris: agree, eviction should be scoped. global evict is dangerous.
security-bot: NOTE: any design touching immediate revocation must be covered by the incident playbook. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/revocation
Devon: another concern: API keys. currently API keys are long-lived and resolved at gateway then cached as actor assertions. If API key is disabled we rely on same invalidation channel.
Sasha: option: make API keys ephemeral (short TTL) + rotate automation. but that forces clients to handle refresh.
Alex: could introduce a 'revoked_at' timestamp in the authz graph and include it in cache entries; validation checks current time vs revoked_at before honoring entry.
Hao: that still needs propagation of revoked_at to edges quickly. so same push path.
Chris: performance test plan: run QPS 10k with TTL 30s vs push invalidation at 100 revokes/min. measure backend QPS and p99.
Maria: policy question: do we want immediate revocation SLA? propose tiered: Enterprise customers get near-immediate (<=1s) for admin revokes via dedicated push channels; others get eventual (<=30s).
Devon: fine, but need to document in API docs and console. also implement audit logs for revoke events.
Sasha: infra tasks: (1) change-proxy produce scoped evict messages w/ rev id, (2) edge consumer + eviction logic w/ revision check, (3) fallbacks: if edge fails to process push, it falls back to TTL expiry.
Hao: security task: ensure events are signed (HMAC) and edge verifies to avoid malicious evicts.
security-bot: CHECKLIST: HMAC signing, replay-protection (nonce or rev id), audit trail.
Chris: small implementation detail: evict route example — `POST /internal/authz/evict` body {"target":"user:U123","scope":"org:O45","rev":9876,"sig":"..."}. edge validates and removes matching cache keys.
Alex: for testing we should create a harness that simulates 100k edge nodes to ensure scale of change-proxy fanout.
Maria: last: RBAC model changes — if we add role inheritance we must include change-delta computation so invalidations are minimal (don't evict entire org on a leaf role change).
Devon: agreed. compute diff and emit fine-grained evicts.
Sasha: action items: Sasha/Hao pair to prototype push invalidation + rev-id compare; Chris to design perf test; Maria to draft SLA wording; Alex to prototype fanout harness.
Devon: thanks — ping in two days with a short status update. :thumbsup:
